question: Will the DDR5 16Gb (2Gx8) spot session average be higher on September 4, 2026 than on August 21, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if the "Session Average" price for "DDR5 16Gb (2Gx8) 4800/5600" shown on the TrendForce DRAM spot price page (https://www.trendforce.com/price/dram/, under the DRAM Spot Price table) as of the final update on September 4, 2026 (GMT+8) is strictly greater than 54.10 (the Session Average recorded on August 21, 2026). It resolves NO if that value is less than or equal to 54.10. Values are US dollars per 16Gb die (for example, a Session Average of 55.500 resolves YES; a value of 54.10 or 53.200 resolves NO).
reference_class: Next-session changes in the TrendForce mainstream DDR5 16Gb (2Gx8) spot Session Average during the Aug-Sep 2026 plateau regime, conditioned on the current level sitting $0.10 (~0.19%) below the threshold
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.38, 0.37, 0.39] -> 0.380; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.38)]
Direct read of the resolution instrument (trendforce.com/price/dram/, update stamped 2026-09-03 18:10 GMT+8) puts the mainstream DDR5 16Gb (2Gx8) 4800/5600 Session Average at 54.00, -0.46% on the day — $0.10 below the 54.10 threshold with a single session remaining. Reference class: one-session-ahead moves in this series, which has gone sideways since Aug 21 (54.10 -> 54.00 over ~9 sessions) after a large Feb-Aug run-up; recent observed daily changes are +0.31%, ~+0.31%, -0.46%, implying SD ~0.5%/session and drift near zero. YES needs +0.19% or better, ~0.4 SD against with essentially no local drift, giving ~0.37. The bullish macro backdrop (DDR4 contract +4.17% Aug, Q3 PC DRAM contract forecast raised to +18-23%, supplier hikes 23-28%) argues for positive drift, but spot has demonstrably not carried it for two weeks, so I apply only a small upward nudge. Adjustments: ~5% chance no Sep 4 update posts before the 12:00Z cutoff (carries forward 54.00 -> NO); ~10% weight on the derivative aggregator memoryindex.io showing 54.24 for Sep 3, which if correct would make a flat day resolve YES. No human prediction market exists on DRAM spot prices at any venue (searched Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers — none found), so there is no anchor to blend. Blended: 0.38.
what_would_change_my_mind: A Sep 3 final intraday update revising the Session Average above 54.10, or confirmation that 54.24 (not 54.00) is the true Sep 3 close
A supplier/contract headline on Sep 3-4 (Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron quote hike, allocation cut) that historically moves spot >1% next session
Evidence that the series is much stickier than assumed — e.g. a run of sessions with |change| < 0.1%, which would push probability further toward NO given the deficit
TrendForce failing to post a Sep 4 update (forces carry-forward of a sub-threshold value)

missing_evidence: No daily table of Session Average values for Aug 22 - Sep 2 was retrievable, so the intra-window path (and true session-change volatility) is inferred from three points; the Aug 21 = 54.10 comparison value is unverifiable outside the criteria text; TrendForce's intraday update schedule is undocument

question: What will Moderna (MRNA) stock close at on Friday, September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the official closing price of Moderna, Inc. common stock (Nasdaq: MRNA) for the regular trading session on Friday, September 4, 2026, in US dollars per share, as reported on the Yahoo Finance historical data page (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MRNA/history/). For example, a closing price of $145.13 resolves as 145.13. If Yahoo Finance is unavailable, the closing price reported by another financial data provider such as Investing.com or MarketWatch, or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), will be used.
reference_class: One-trading-day-ahead closing price of a large-cap biotech in the weeks after a binary clinical readout, with ~90-110% annualized implied vol
dispersion_basis: daily log-return SD 6.0% (blend of post-event realized 6.9% ex the Aug-20 -24% unwind day, and 30d ATM IV ~88% => 5.5%/day) x 2.56 x 148.4
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs: medians 148.4/148/148.3 -> 148.2; the narrative below is the research run's own view]
One trading day of variance from a known anchor: MRNA closed $148.87 on Sep 3, 2026 (stockanalysis.com and investing.com agree on the full OHLC; the Sep 2 close of $150.81 chains correctly to Benzinga's report). Reference class is one-day-ahead close for a large-cap biotech in a post-binary-event high-vol regime; the class implies the prior close is the median and dispersion comes from the regime's daily sigma, not from a directional view. Sigma: realized post-event daily SD is ~6.9% excluding the Aug-20 -24% unwind, ~10.7% including it; options imply ~5.5%/day at 88% IV. I use 6.0%, reflecting decaying but still extreme vol (Sep 1 +9.9%, Sep 2 -2.2%, Sep 3 -1.3%). Median nudged fractionally below the close (148.4) for a mildly negative after-hours print, three consecutive down days, a fresh Rothschild downgrade to Sell (Sep 3), and convert-arb hedging pressure from the $2.6bn Aug-28 note deal; against that, no scheduled Sep 4 catalyst and pre-holiday drift is near zero, so the tilt is deliberately tiny. Escape masses omitted: reaching <60 needs -60% in a day (and the fine print backstops a halt with the $148.87 prior close, inside range), and >260 needs +75%, which would require an unscheduled takeover bid priced by Polymarket at ~1% for the whole of 2026. Caveat: several search snippets quoted stale/garbled Sep 3 figures ($144.54, $150.34); I weight the two structured historical tables.

missing_evidence: The Sep 4-expiry implied volatility / straddle-implied expected move could not be retrieved (OptionCharts paywalled), so the width rests on realized vol plus a 30-day IV quote rather than the actual one-day option price; no borrow-rate or short-interest data on the convert hedge.
